## Findings from the references

I looked at all four attachments.

- **LUCA** is a printed sheet with one reading column. Prices sit in a stable right-hand column. Groups are separated by air and small spaced caps. The only picture is a continuous narrow strip down the left edge, away from the text.
- **Osip** uses almost no chrome: centred lines, and vertical gaps that change from group to group. Type and space do all the work, and there are no cards or badges.
- **Our current four** (before-desktop and before-mobile) are the same image-then-text card list in different colours. The 01 and 04 desktop captures are two columns of large photos, and mobile is a 3:2 photo above a title, a boxed price, a description and a button. Mobile is mostly photo, so the dish names and prices are far apart. In every variant the photo comes first and the price is a boxed chip.

I cannot see dishes 3 and 4 in the screenshots. The layouts will depend on DOM order and on the filter state, never on category names.

## Four chosen directions

| | Parent | Composition | What carries the page |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | WhiteInk | **Printed sheet with a photo strip.** Each dish is a row with a small-caps category label, the Georgia name, a dotted leader and a right-aligned tabular price, then the description and the details. Each dish's photo is the left cell of its row, with no gaps between rows. On desktop the four photos therefore join into one continuous tall strip down the left edge, as on the LUCA sheet. On mobile the photo becomes a short 16:7 band above the row. | Price column and leader line |
| 02 | Masthead Vermilion | **Newspaper front page.** The first dish is the lead story: a big photo beside a huge condensed vermilion name and a large price. The other three are narrow columns separated by vertical rules, with a small 3:2 photo, name and price. There is a heavy rule at the top, and the price sits in a vermilion block. On mobile it is a single stack with the lead first. | Lead vs. columns, rules |
| 03 | Brasa | **Widescreen frames.** Each dish is a full-width black frame with a 21:9 photo, like a reel still. Under each photo is one caption line in three parts: a wide uppercase Syne name, the description and details, and the price large in ember. Frames are separated by hairlines and have no card chrome. | Cinematic scale, ember price |
| 04 | Herbario | **Centred specimen column.** A narrow column about 34rem wide on a paper mat. Each dish has a small 4:5 plate, a centred Bodoni name, an italic category line, a centred description, then the price with a fine wine rule above it. The vertical gaps between dishes alternate (tight, then loose), which is the Osip lesson. The details disclosure is also centred. | Centred axis, whitespace rhythm |

## Source plan

All changes sit in the existing Astro/CSS renderer.

- **New `src/components/composition/MenuCollection.astro`.**
  - It renders the same OfferingCollection semantics as the `ContextualModule` branch.
  - That covers the section attributes (`data-module-id`, `data-component`, `data-scope-id`, `data-required`, `data-semantic-page`) and every `data-fact-id` and `data-fact-scope`.
  - It also keeps `data-offering-id`, `data-offering-scope` and `data-search`, the `[data-menu-tools] hidden` block with `[data-menu-search]`, `[data-menu-category]` and `[data-menu-count]`, `.contextual-collection`, the `<details class="dish-detail">`, the `?plato=` selection links, the noscript note and the `ContextualImage` bindings.
  - The module title (h2) and the introduction stay. Only the layout operator and a `data-menu-layout` value (`ledger`, `front-page`, `frames` or `plate`) differ.
  - I drop the `01 / La carta de ejemplo` kicker and the `0{i+1} /` decoration, because both are on your ban list.
- **New `src/design/menu-carta.css`.**
  - It is imported with `?raw` and scoped under `.page-collection [data-menu-layout=…]`, so it never touches other routes.
  - It is appended to the emitted style only when `page.kind==='collection'`.
  - Filtered or empty states reset to a simple single column. There are no container min-heights or container-level borders and no ghost decoration, so a filtered single dish or an empty list leaves no gap.
- **`ExperienceComposition.astro`:** append the CSS and render `MenuCollection` for `collection` only. It reads `art ?? p.hero` to pick the layout.
- **`ArtisticPages.astro`:** the collection branch calls `MenuCollection` the same way.
- **Unchanged:** the selection page (`pedidos`), `ContextualModule`, the other CSS and the client JS. Because `MenuCollection` copies the existing DOM contract, `experience-refinement-client.ts` should keep working untouched.

## Constraints I'll hold to

- Controls are 44px and body text is at least 14px at 4.5:1 contrast. Prices use `tabular-nums`.
- Nothing overlays text on a photo.
- Everything is static by default, with no motion.
- 360px has no horizontal overflow.
- Focus rings come from the existing `--focus` token.
- I override the existing `.collection-item` and `.contextual-collection` rules only with higher-specificity selectors inside the new stylesheet. I do not edit the shared rules.

## Uncertainties and risks

- Any tests or snapshots that assert the old kicker, the `0N /` numbers or the card DOM order on the carta pages will see a deliberate difference. Please check them.
- `ContextualImage` has fixed `sizes` attributes, so the 01 strip and 03 frames may load a larger source than they display. I would leave it alone, because changing it could alter other pages' HTML.
- I have not rendered anything. Visual tuning of leaders, strip crops and the 21:9 crop of the pizza and pasta photos needs your browser captures.

Waiting for your feedback before I edit.
